name: In-situ cryogenic nanobeam electron diffraction of CDW melting in 1T-TiSe2 nanoflakes from 20 K through the 210-230 K bulk transition
plain_name: Watch charge-density-wave order melt in tiny flakes inside a cooled electron microscope
description: Liquid-exfoliated 1T-TiSe2 nanoflakes on TEM grids are cooled to 20 K (liquid-helium flow holder) or 100 K (liquid-nitrogen holder), then warmed in 10-20 K steps to room temperature while 2x2 superlattice peaks are tracked by nanobeam electron diffraction at 60 kV, revealing melting-point depression for flakes below 100 nm effective radius.
keywords: Watch charge-density-wave order melt in tiny flakes inside a cooled electron microscope

sources.citation: Siddique S., Kiani M. T., Lesser O., et al., Cha J. J. Melting point depression of charge density wave in 1T-TiSe2 due to size effects. arXiv:2509.16730 (2025)

requirements.rationale: The smallest flakes only order (or are shown not to order) at the 20 K base temperature of the liquid-helium holder.
Warming must pass through the bulk CDW transition (210-230 K) to locate each flake's melting temperature.
Optional: the 20 K base was reached with continuous liquid-helium flow.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
